steps.content: A last, mournful wail escapes the creature as it tumbles down.
Its body unravels into smoke, dissolving into wisps of black mist, slowly swallowed by the brightening void of the rift.
Cleansed, the rift itself begins to reveal its true form.

steps.speaker: Kisugi Ai
steps.content: Rui! Hitomi! Look! The white light... is still there!
With an excited bounce, Kisugi Ai grabs her sisters' hands and pulls them eagerly toward the light.
You make no move to follow, staying rooted in place.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Step into the light, and you should be able to return home.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Once you leave, the rift here will disappear… and I will return to DisCity.
Up ahead, the three sisters come to a halt. As one, they turn to look back at you.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I'm glad I got to meet you all. And thank you... for the wonderful coffee.

steps.speaker: Kisugi Rui
steps.content: The feeling is mutual. And please, accept our apologies for the trouble we've caused.

steps.speaker: Kisugi Hitomi
steps.content: You're quite an interesting person. Your companions are remarkable, too. If fate allows, I'd welcome another serious competition with Miss Rabbit and Miss Fox.

steps.speaker: Kisugi Ai
steps.content: Could you... say goodbye to Wynn, Eugene... and Tetra for me?
She lowers her head, then quickly lifts it again.

steps.speaker: Kisugi Ai
steps.content: Tell them... even though I was always worried about getting home, being with them made me really happy.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I'll tell them. I promise.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: And I hope everything goes well for you, back in your world.
You wave to the three sisters, bidding them farewell, and watch as they fade into the light.
Kisugi Rui is the final one to go. With one foot poised to enter, she glances over her shoulder.

steps.speaker: Kisugi Rui
steps.content: Though our time together was brief, Chief, feeling the full weight of this power made me realize something.

steps.speaker: Kisugi Rui
steps.content: Your shackles... they're warm. Through them, we felt your kindness. Your resolve.

steps.speaker: Kisugi Rui
steps.content: But they would also leave you to endure a painful life in that cruel city.

steps.speaker: Kisugi Hitomi
steps.content: We're just passing travelers from another world. We probably have no right to say this...

steps.speaker: Kisugi Hitomi
steps.content: But I'll say it anyway.

steps.speaker: Kisugi Hitomi
steps.content: May you always stand firm in what you believe. And protect everything precious to you.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Thank you, travelers from another world.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: And I wish for you to stay as radiant as the angels you sought. May you find every treasure you're looking for.

steps.speaker: Kisugi Hitomi
steps.content: Then... goodbye.
The final silhouette melts into the light. The radiant portal itself contracts, shrinking to a pinprick before vanishing.
Around you, the unstable rift shudders violently, its Mania-saturated structure buckling in on itself.
You shut your eyes, bracing for the end of the journey.
After another nauseating spin, you land with a soft thud on damp, fragrant soil.
When you open your eyes, skyscrapers surround you. But at your feet is a resilient scrap of urban wilderness holding its ground.
Above, through the urban haze, a clear patch of night sky opens, and it sparkles with the same impossible brilliance as the cosmos you gazed upon together within the rift.
A Few Days Later
The incident with the otherworld visitors keeps you up late for days on end, handling all the aftermath and filing reports.
Today, the pace finally breaks.
With both hands, you lift a coffee cup to your lips, drinking in the warmth and the quiet. As you lower the empty cup, a sigh escapes you.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Ahh... I'm really going to miss their coffee.
As you open a drawer to resume your report, a familiar card catches your eye. It's resting right on top of your notebook.
You remember how Kisugi Rui slipped it into your pocket as she said goodbye on that last day.
Back then, you were too busy helping them cross back home to look at it.
You pick it up—their signature calling card, white with a red cat-shaped pattern.
It reads:
"Chief, we're really glad we met you. If fate allows it, I hope... our paths cross again."
A few days later, a grainy photo spreading across the web has reignited heated debate throughout Eastside.

Some say the phantom thieves known as CAT'S EYE had stolen the Otherland Angels. Others claim they are Bureau operatives all along, and that the whole affair has been a coordinated sting to bring the Marauders to justice.

The photo rides the wave of public fascination for two full days before finally receding. In its wake, under the dual scrutiny of the Public Security Bureau and the Bureau, Eastside's art collectors become markedly less inclined to advertise their treasures as challenges for thieves.

Time, as it always does, begins to soften the edges of memory. The legend of the phantom thieves known as CAT'S EYE fades, as does the recollection of the cozy little café that briefly served as their stage.
And so, at the close of this tale, let us pour a final cup. May we all find the things worthy of our love.
